chain.label: Carson Helicopters understated the helicopter's empty weight in the weight-and-balance records given to the pilots
chain.trigger: the intentional understatement of the helicopter's empty weight

chain.label: Carson Helicopters distributed an altered takeoff power available chart (2.5-minute OEI graph pasted into RFMS #8 Figure 4)
chain.trigger: the alteration of the power available chart to exaggerate the helicopter's lift capability

chain.label: PIC used unapproved above-minimum-specification torque in the load calculations, per a Carson Helicopters procedure
chain.trigger: the practice of using unapproved above-minimum specification torque in performance calculations

chain.label: Insufficient USFS and FAA oversight of Carson Helicopters' weights, charts and Part 135 compliance
chain.trigger: insufficient oversight by the USFS and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)

chain.label: High density altitude at H-44 with no headwind benefit (6,106 ft PA, 23 C, DA 8,476 ft, calm)
chain.trigger: The temperature, PA, and wind speed at H-44 for the accident takeoff were estimated at 23° C, 6,106 feet, and calm... The calculated DA was 8,476 feet.

chain.label: Confined ridgetop helispot at ~6,000 ft with 50-foot trees along the departure path
chain.trigger: Fifty-foot trees were directly ahead of the LZ.

chain.label: Crew experience base in logging and water-dropping work, where operating to engine topping is routine and loads are jettisonable
chain.trigger: they were accustomed to operating at the limit of the helicopter's performance

chain.label: Helicopter loaded to 19,008 lbs, at or beyond its actual HOGE capability, on load calculations that overstated allowable payload by 3,437 lbs
chain.trigger: these discrepancies resulted in overestimating the helicopter's maximum allowable payload by 3,437 lbs

caused_by.evidence: the empty weight of the helicopter was 13,845 lbs, which was 1,437 lbs heavier than the empty weight of 12,408 lbs that CHSI provided to the accident helicopter's pilots
the altered takeoff (5-minute) power available chart that was provided by Carson Helicopters eliminated a safety margin of 1,200 lbs of emergency reserve power
Using above-min spec torque equated to an additional 800-lb increase in the calculated HOGE weight capability
effective oversight would likely have identified that Carson Helicopters was using improper weight and performance charts for contract bidding and actual load calculations
the accident takeoff was unsuccessful because the helicopter was loaded with more weight than it could carry in a HOGE given the ambient conditions

chain.label: Crew did not address the engines reaching topping and rotor droop on the two prior departures from H-44
chain.trigger: The CVR did not record any discussion by the pilots regarding the fact that the engines had reached topping.

caused_by.evidence: the pilots likely recognized that the helicopter was approaching its maximum performance capability on the two prior departures from H-44 but elected to proceed
the topping of the engines indicated that the helicopter was laboring to fly and was close to its absolute performance capability

chain.label: Pilots elected to depart H-44 with a 2,565-lb payload, judging the helicopter had performance in excess of the load calculation
chain.trigger: the copilot confirmed that the helicopter was "good to go"

caused_by.evidence: the pilots believed the helicopter was 'good to go' with capability beyond that required to HOGE
neither pilot called attention to the discrepancy between the predicted and actual performance of the helicopter or suggested postponing further flight

chain.label: Power required exceeded power available; engines pinned at topping, rotor speed drooped and the helicopter could not climb out of ground effect
chain.trigger: Between 1940:46 and 1941:31, the N drooped from 106.9 to 95.0 percent... reaching a final value of 93.5 percent

caused_by.evidence: At 1940:46, the PIC began to increase the power for takeoff

the power required from the engines to climb and maintain N exceeded the power available, not as a result of a power loss due to engine malfunction but due to excessive power demands associated with attempting to lift more weight than possible in a HOGE

chain.label: Fuel tanks certified to 1961 CAR 7 standards and not crash resistant, releasing fuel on impact
chain.trigger: the immediate, intense fire that resulted from the spillage of fuel upon impact from the fuel tanks that were not crash resistant

chain.label: Cabin seats and their floor attachments not crash resistant, meeting only CAR 7.260 load limits
chain.trigger: the separation from the floor of the cabin seats that were not crash resistant

chain.label: Cabin restraints fitted with an unfamiliar rotary release buckle that passengers could not operate after the crash
chain.trigger: the use of an inappropriate release mechanism on the cabin seat restraints

chain.label: Main rotor blades and fuselage struck trees along the departure path
chain.trigger: The helicopter collided with the trees

caused_by.evidence: the helicopter began to move forward and then began losing altitude as it continued down slope
the main rotor blades were not high enough to clear the trees

chain.label: Helicopter impacted down-sloping terrain and came to rest on its left side
chain.trigger: subsequently impacted the down sloping terrain, coming to rest on its left side

caused_by.evidence: Debris began to fly from the surrounding trees and the helicopter settled into the vegetation.

chain.label: Immediate postcrash fire; nine occupants fatally injured and four seriously injured
chain.trigger: The pilot-in-command, the safety crewmember, and seven firefighters were fatally injured; the copilot and three firefighters were seriously injured.

caused_by.evidence: Almost immediately after the impact, witnesses saw smoke and fire coming from the wreckage.
the postcrash fire likely originated from the ignition of the fuel that was released or spilled from the helicopter's fuel tanks
the majority of the cabin seats that were occupied during the crash separated from the floor... hindering their ability to evacuate the cabin
the surviving firefighters were unable to release the rotary restraints under emergency conditions because they were unfamiliar with the rotary-release mechanism
